chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me, saying: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad 'Isa, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, and Ya'qub ibn Yazid, all from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from someone whose name he mentioned, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Ismail, about whom Allah, the Exalted, said in His Book: 'And mention in the Book Ismail. Indeed, he was truthful in his promise, and he was a messenger, and a prophet' — this was not Ismail, the son of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). He was a prophet among the prophets whom Allah sent to his people. They captured him and skinned the scalp of his head and his face. An angel came to him from Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, and said, 'Indeed, Allah has sent me to you, so order me to do whatever you wish.' He said to me, 'I am an example for what will be done to al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلَ: Ismail (a specific prophet distinguished from the son of Ibrahim)

ai.seo_question: Who is the Ismail mentioned in the Quran who was skinned, and how does he relate to Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a.s.) distinctive interpretation that the 'Ismail' praised in Surah Maryam as a 'truthful promise' and 'messenger' is not the son of Ibrahim, but a separate prophet martyred by skinning. This unique identification establishes a direct typological link (uswah) between this prophet’s physical suffering and the martyrdom of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), reinforcing the theological significance of Husayn’s sacrifice as a continuation of prophetic trials.
